summary: CRC-style checksum over a byte buffer using two 16-bit accumulators seeded from a1 and the reduction constant 0xFFF1. Processes the buffer in chunks of up to 5552 bytes with a 16-byte unrolled inner loop plus a residual byte loop, folding both accumulators modulo 0xFFF1 between chunks, and returns (high accumulator << 16) | low accumulator. Returns 1 instead when the buffer pointer is null.

operations.description: Initialize the buffer pointer v3 to a2 and split the seed a1 into two 16-bit accumulators: v4 = (unsigned __int16)a1 (low) and v5 = HIWORD(a1) (high).
If the buffer pointer a2 is null, return 1 immediately.
Outer loop iterates while remaining byte count a3 is non-zero.
Per chunk, process min(a3, 5552) bytes (0x15B0): v7 defaults to 5552 and is clamped to a3 when a3 < 0x15B0, then a3 is decremented by v7.

When the chunk size is at least 16, run an unrolled 16-byte inner loop: a chain of additions folds each byte into the running v4/v5 accumulators, advancing the pointer by 16 per iteration and repeating v7 >> 4 times.
Residual bytes of the chunk (fewer than 16 after the unrolled loop) are folded one at a time: v4 += *v3++, then v5 += v4.
Reduce both accumulators modulo 0xFFF1: v4 %= 0xFFF1 at the end of each chunk body and v5 %= 0xFFF1 in the outer loop increment.

clean_pseudocode: do { fold 16 bytes into v4/v5; v3 += 16; } while (--blocks);
